


                     B I L D S C H I R M   T R I X
                   =================================
                    Vintage Computing Festival 2015
                                Edition


Preface
==========================

During my time travel through the lost computerworld I came across
"Bildschirmtext", an information system based on a technology called
"Videotex". Videotex looks similar to the Teletext system you know
well from your TV-Set. However. Videotex has some extra capabilities.
It is an interactive medium that allows direct interaction with a 
computersystem. It has limited graphic capabilites. A user can define
own character tiles and custom colors. With some tricks even 
animations are possible. I find Videotex an exciting and beautiful
media.

Today the entire videotex-world with all its colorful, pixelized 
information pages is lost. Everything is gone. However, here and
there one can find some leftover Terminals. How sad, I thought,
but what if we could create a new backhaul for these?

I started researching the Interface, got the ETSI-Specifications and
after a few month I had my own videotex-backhaul running. This 
package contains the outcome of my research and everything you need
to start an own CEPT TCD 6-1/ETS 300 072 videotex-service.




This disribution includes:
==========================

1) ./doc	(Some Documentation, download ETSI specs yourself)
2) ./gcc	The avr-gcc compiler needed to compile the microPAD 
                firmware
3) ./mikroPAD	A modern ip-modem version of the dbt03
4) ./miniBTX	An adapter to connect any dbt03 compatible terminal
                to your PC
		(Also includes some software tools)
5) ./pcPAD	The mikroPAD as a PC software for use with miniBTX
6) ./srv	A bunch of Videotex-Pages to start off
7) ./tools	Some tools to help you athoring own Videotex-Pages



Copyright / License
==========================

This is an open-source project. The entire system with its hardware
and software falls under the GNU General Public License (See
LICENSE.txt for details)

However, for the Videotex-Pages in ./srv do not fall under GPL.
Here I make the following exception: All my Videotex-Pages are
public domain. I will not claim any copyright for this work,
you can freely copy and edit the pages and create a new
beautiful artwork from it. 

If you still have Bildschirmtext content somewhere you wish to
donate you can contact me via email. Send me whatever you have,
diskettes, old backups, screenshots. I will then see if I have 
the time to restore the content.

If you use some of my BTX work for your own projects. I would like
